info.title: SplatterVault Studio API
info.description:
The routes your game and your backend call: player sign-in (platform proofs, SplatterVault email accounts and guests), player data (each player's saved data and the game's data), the store (virtual currencies, items, purchases) and the game-server session and billing routes the Unity SDK calls (its account sign-in routes are in the full reference at `/docs`).

**Credentials.** The game client sends a player token from a sign-in (`Authorization: Bearer <player token>`, about an hour; refresh or sign in again). Your backend sends an organization API key (`X-API-Key: sv_org_...`) holding the route's permission: never put one in a game build. Sign-in exchanges, the public keys and a game's public data need no credential. Each operation lists what it accepts.

**Errors.** Studio routes refuse with `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<sentence>" }` (some player data refusals add `details`): key your handling on `error`, show `message`. Each response lists the codes it may carry; the set is open, so handle an unknown code by its HTTP status. Every 429 carries `Retry-After`, and so does a 503 `data_busy`. Every answer is `Cache-Control: no-store` unless it says otherwise.

Codes any studio route may answer, listed on each route by name: `unauthorized` (401, an `X-API-Key` was sent that is not a valid key), `banned` (403, the address or account is banned from SplatterVault; `details` holds its `type` and `scopes`), `forbidden` (403, on a change: a browser sent a website sign-in cookie without the CSRF header; send no cookies), `bad_request` (400, the body is not a JSON object), `internal_error` (500, try again later) and `not_found` (404, no such route). Player routes add `token_invalid`, `token_expired` and `player_deleted` (401: sign in again), `rate_limited` (429, 60 requests a minute per player, whatever the token or game) and `player_sign_in_disabled` (503).

**Changes.** Store changes take an `Idempotency-Key` header: send the same key again to retry safely.

playerToken.description: A player token from a /player-auth sign-in: `Authorization: Bearer <player token>`. Only the player routes accept it; it expires after about an hour (sign in or refresh again).

orgApiKey.name: X-API-Key
orgApiKey.description: An organization API key (`sv_org_...`) holding the route's permission, for its own organization's games and players. Keep it on your backend: never in a game build.

personalApiKey.name: X-API-Key
personalApiKey.description: A personal API key (`sv_...`): acts as you. Refused by the studio routes.

websiteSession.description: A SplatterVault account's access token (the website sign-in): `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>`.

error.description: A stable code: key your handling on it. An open set: each response lists the codes it may carry (and x-error-codes holds them as a list); handle any other code by the HTTP status, as new ones may be added.

message.description: A plain sentence for people. It never carries a token, a proof or a platform's answer; do not parse it.

details.description: Some player data refusals say more: which op, store or key (version_conflict: [{ store, key, version }]), or which limit (limit_exceeded: { limit, max }).

StudioError.description: What every studio route answers when it refuses a request. Every answer is Cache-Control: no-store.

name.description: The error's kind, e.g. NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, BAD_REQUEST.

errors.description: Validation details, when there are any.

PlatformError.description: The refusal of the game-server session routes (website and Unity SDK routes), except a platform ban (PlatformBanRefusal).

banned.description: Always true: tells this answer from PlatformError.

type.description: What is banned: ip (the address the request came from) or email (the account).

scopes.description: The ban's scopes; FULL_PLATFORM refuses every route.

PlatformBanRefusal.description: The 403 a game-server session route answers when the address or account is banned from SplatterVault (before any route runs). Studio routes answer a ban as StudioError banned instead.

ImportStatus.description: created, updated and unchanged were applied (or would be, in a dry run); conflict and invalid were not.

provider.description: The system that knows the player by providerId.

providerId.description: The player's id in that system.

providerApp.description: The app of that system: xsolla Login project id, PlayFab title id, Supabase project ref.

PlayerRef.description: A player named by an id another system knows them by.

IdentityProvider.description: A way a player signs in.

id.description: The player's SplatterVault id. Store it: every player route and the studio routes name players by it.

newPlayer.description: True when this sign-in created the player.

token.description: The player token (a JWT signed with Ed25519, about an hour). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to the player routes; game servers and studio backends can verify it offline with GET /player-auth/keys.

expiresAt.description: When the token stops working: sign in (or refresh) again before then.

refreshToken.description: Keep it on the device: POST /player-auth/refresh trades it for a new player token. Single-use.

deviceSecret.description: Shown ONCE. Keep it on the device: POST /player-auth/device signs the guest in with it.

refreshToken.description: Only after an email CHANGE: every other device was signed out; keep this one's new refresh token.

resendAfterSeconds.description: How long to wait before asking for another one (60).

CodeSent.description: Answered whether or not a code was sent (an address without an account learns nothing).

kid.description: Key id: the token header's kid names it.

PlayerTokenKeys.description: A JWKS: the current key, and during a rotation the next and the previous one.

slaveIp.description: The server's address, once it is up.

ready.description: True once readyAt is set: the game server has said it is ready for players at least once (its ready signal, or the start of a match). It stays true after the session stops.

readyAt.description: When the game server first said it was ready for players (its ready signal, or the start of a match). Null until then; set once and never moved, so it stays set after the session stops.

readyDeadlineAt.description: When the game server is expected to be ready by: the moment its server was up (it registered, or a pool server was claimed) plus 300 seconds. Null until the server is up. Recorded only: nothing acts on a missed deadline.

region.description: A region code, or AUTO to pick the closest to playerIps.

organizationId.description: Bill the organization (an organization API key fills it in).

channel.description: Use the build deployed to this channel.

autoDestroyOnProcessExit.description: Stop the session when the game process exits.

idleTimeoutMinutes.description: Stop after this many minutes with no connections (5-1440).

playerIps.description: Region AUTO only: the players' addresses (never stored).

ttlSeconds.description: Release the server after this many seconds.

connection.description: null until the server is reachable.

tags.description: Sign your players in from the game client, without a SplatterVault account: a platform proof (Xsolla, Meta Quest, Steam, PlayFab, Supabase), a SplatterVault email account or a guest. The answer is a player token (about an hour) for the player routes, verifiable offline with GET /player-auth/keys.

tags.name: Player data
tags.description: Each player's saved data (the player store is theirs to write, readonly is yours) and the game's public data, for the game client (player token). The public data needs no credential.

tags.name: Store
tags.description: The game client's store: the catalog, the player's balances and items and history, buying with virtual currency, using items up, and Meta Quest purchases. Every change takes an Idempotency-Key.

tags.name: Player data (studio backend)
tags.description: Read and write any player's data and the game's data from your backend, resolve your ids to player ids, import, and follow erased players. An organization API key only.

tags.name: Player sign-in (studio backend)
tags.description: Your backend signs players in with your own ids, erases players, and imports player lists. An organization API key only: never put one in a game build.

tags.name: Store (studio backend)
tags.description: Give, take, sell and reverse from your backend; read any player's balances, items and history; import a catalog or players' holdings. An organization API key only. Every change takes an Idempotency-Key.

tags.name: Game-server sessions
tags.description: Start, list, rename, reschedule and stop game-server sessions paid with credits or a subscription, claim a warm server from a pool, and read the launch arguments a session may set: the routes the Unity SDK calls. A website sign-in, a personal API key or an organization API key; these routes refuse in the platform's own error shape (PlatformError), and a platform ban as PlatformBanRefusal (403).
